title: catTFRE mass spectrometry analysis reveals transcription factor network driver of Osteosarcoma
projectDescription: we used the catTFRE to fish out transcription factor subpopulation of Osteosarcoma nuclear extract for mass spectrometry analysis.
sampleProcessingProtocol: a total of 110 transcription factor binding sites (TFBS) linked by linkers were cloned into the pUC57 plasmid (Genscript, SD1176), matching a control plasmid with a reduced number of TFBS. The catTFREs plasmid was amplified, linearized from the backbone, and biotinylated for downstream applications. The catTFREs construct was immobilized on DynabeadsTM M-280 Streptavidin (Invitrogen, 11206D) by incubating for 3 hours on a rotator at 4 °C following the manufacturer’s instructions. Beads were washed to remove unbound DNA and nonspecific binding, then mixed with nuclear protein extract at a ratio of 100 μg protein to 5 μg DNA. The sample of pull-down reactions was incubated for 4 hours, then rinsed three times with HEPES (pH 7.5), supplemented with 200 mM NaCl and protein inhibitor, and eluted in 20 mM ammonium bicarbonate for mass spectrometry analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: Samples were analysed by LS-MC timsTOF Pro (Bruker Daltonik, Germany) and searched against the human Uniprot database using PEAKS X+ version 10 (Bioinformatics Solutions, Canada). The following parameters were applied: digestion enzyme: trypsin; maximum missed cleavage: 1; fragment ion mass error tolerance: 0.03 Da; parent ion error tolerance: 15.0 ppm; fixed modifications: carbamidomethylation, maximum number of PTMs: 2, and false-discovery rate: 1%.
